# Stub 1.14 (source-maps) — spec review

Audit of `backend/apps/stubs/source_maps/` against
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-18-VULN-SCANNING-COOK-BOOK/01-information-gathering/14-source-maps.md`.

## Process anomaly — spec enrichment skipped

Unlike 1.10–1.13, the **spec body is the un-enriched GPT-5.5 placeholder** (71 lines, all `<!-- comments -->` under empty `##` headings). The matching plan file is also placeholder. The implementation shipped over 7 slices (`2d39f72`…`3b0b11e` + simplify rounds `e37fadc`, `28eba16`) against a contract the author carried in their head — visible only as inline `Spec §"X"` references inside the code.

**Implication:** the standard "audit the implementation as a translation of the spec markdown" cannot run — the source-of-truth document is empty. This review substitutes a **three-axis audit**:

1. The implementation's internal coherence (does the code do what its own docstrings and tests claim).
2. Conformance with the [shared schema](../superpowers/specs/2026-05-18-VULN-SCANNING-COOK-BOOK/00-shared-schema.md) and the patterns set by enriched stubs 1.10–1.13.
3. Source-maps domain best practice (cross-origin discipline, comment + fallback paths, v3 metadata extraction, etc.).

A backfill of the implicit contract is captured under [Implicit contract — backfill](#implicit-contract--backfill) below so a future enrichment pass (or another agent) has somewhere to start.

## Compliant

### Detection logic

- **Read-only HTTP.** `fetcher.fetch_url` only calls `client.get()`. No POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/OPTIONS anywhere in the runner.
- **No request body, no credentials.** httpx defaults; no `Authorization`, cookie, or `Accept` header beyond library default.
- **Redirect discipline.** `follow_redirects=True`, `max_redirects=3` (spec-style cap). `TooManyRedirects` caught alongside `TransportError` → `inconclusive`. Final-URL origin compared via shared `_shared/url.origin`; mismatch → `inconclusive` so an off-host map body never lands as evidence.
- **Body cap.** `FetcherConfig.max_body_bytes=2_000_000` enforced at `fetcher._classify`.
- **Asset enumeration is closed-form.** `parser.parse_html_assets` walks BS4-parsed HTML for `<script src>`, `<link rel=stylesheet>`, `<link rel=preload as=script>`, `<link rel=modulepreload>`. Cross-origin / `data:` / `blob:` / `javascript:` URLs filtered via `classify_same_origin`. Dedupe + first-seen order. Capped at `max_assets=50`.
- **`sourceMappingURL` extraction.** JS regex matches both `//#` (modern) and `//@` (legacy). CSS regex matches only block-comment form. Cross-form matches rejected — `/*# */` inside JS body and `//# …` inside CSS body both return `None`. Last-match-wins (canonical comment lives at end of file).
- **Resolver discipline.** `resolve_map_url` never makes network calls and never decodes `data:` payloads. Classifies into `{ok, inline_data_url, cross_origin, invalid}` so the runner can emit a spec-compliant candidate for `data:` without fetching, and skip `cross_origin` / `invalid` with a diagnostic.
- **Validator discipline.** `validator.parse_source_map` accepts only top-level objects with `version` AND one of `sources`/`sections`/`mappings`. `sourcesContent` counted, never persisted in `Evidence.data` or `Finding.data` (deliberately) — only `sources_content_count` + `has_sources_content` flag flow forward.
- **Path categoriser is closed-vocabulary.** `path_categories._CATEGORY_ORDER` pins 12 categories; `_INDICATOR_ORDER` pins 11 indicators. Substring-only matching, no parsing, no execution. Output sorted in the canonical order so the persisted row is byte-stable across runs.
- **No AI involvement.** No LLM call, no remote inference. All decision points are deterministic.
- **No hostname → expected-tech leaks.** Detection runs against response bodies / URLs; hostname is never consulted.

### Persistence contract

- **Shared types reused.** `ScanRun`, `ScanTargetRun`, `ScanTarget`, `Evidence`, `Finding`, `EvidenceSource`, `FindingStatus`, `Severity` all imported — none redefined.
- **One `Evidence` row per important GET.** HTML probe always (diagnostic, persisted regardless of outcome), per-asset (SCRIPT | CSS), per-attempted-map (PATH).
- **`Evidence.data`** carries `{kind, status, content_type}` so a future projector can reconstruct the action from the row alone (per [[event-log-medium-done-well]]).
- **One `Finding` per (asset, attempted-map) pair.** Title is `Source map: <finding_status>`, `category="source_maps"` (== `_FINDING_SOURCE`), `data` records `asset_url`, `asset_kind`, `asset_final_url`, `map_url`, `map_reference_type`, `indicators`, `evidence_ids`, and (when present) `map_status`, `map_final_url`, `source_map_version`, `sources_count`, `has_sources_content`, `source_path_samples`, `source_path_categories`, `internal_path_indicators`.
- **Confidence taxonomy** from `_shared/types.Confidence` — `high` (comment-referenced + valid v3), `medium` (fallback-discovered + valid v3), `low` (everything else).
- **`FindingStatus`** uses the shared `{candidate, confirmed, rejected, stale}` enum. `stale` is deferred (needs cross-run state, tracked in commit message).
- **`Severity`** capped at `LOW` even when `sourcesContent` exposed — matches the deliberate cookbook policy ("source-map exposure alone never raises to medium").
- **Append-only semantics inherited from Django `Evidence.save` guard.** No custom unsave in the source_maps runner.
- **Single `transaction.atomic()` wraps each ScanTargetRun pass** so a partial-failure leaves no half-persisted state.

### Pass/fail behaviour (inferred from tests)

| Verdict | Test (in `test_runner.py`) |
|---|---|
| comment-referenced map, valid v3 | `test_comment_referenced_map_yields_confirmed_high` |
| fallback `.map` probe, valid v3 | `test_fallback_map_yields_confirmed_medium` |
| inline `data:` URL | `test_inline_data_url_yields_candidate` |
| 404 on `.map` fallback | `test_404_map_yields_rejected` |
| no assets in HTML | `test_no_assets_in_html_writes_html_evidence_only` |
| HTML fetch failure | `test_html_fetch_failure_writes_diagnostic_evidence` |
| asset fetch failure | `test_asset_fetch_failure_skips_finding` |
| confirmed-path evidence chain | `test_confirmed_finding_persists_three_evidence_rows`, `test_evidence_ids_referenced_on_finding` |

`classify.py` adds 15 verdict-level tests covering the cross-origin / invalid / blocked / malformed / inconclusive paths. `fetcher`, `parser`, `resolver`, `validator` each have ≥15 tests covering the cookbook's parsing edge cases.

**Negative assertions covered:**
- `RejectedFindingTests` confirm 404 maps don't become confirmed findings.
- `_helpers._stamp_url` sentinel makes it hard to accidentally test against an off-host body — cross-origin redirect tests use explicit `url=` overrides.
- `validator.parse_source_map` returns `None` on non-dict, missing-version, no-sources-no-sections-no-mappings, JSON-decode-error inputs — exercised in `test_validator.py`.
- `resolver._is_inline_data_url` blocks decode of `data:` payloads — exercised in `test_resolver.py`.

### Acceptance criteria (verifiable)

- **Deterministic.** No random, no AI, no clock-dependent logic.
- **Bounded.** `max_assets=50`, `max_body_bytes=2_000_000`, `max_redirects=3`, `timeout_seconds=10`.
- **Transport-error tolerant.** `httpx.TransportError`, `httpx.TooManyRedirects` → `inconclusive` with diagnostic Evidence row.
- **Redirect-policy compliant.** Same-origin enforced post-redirect; off-origin final URL → `inconclusive`.

## Deviations / open items

### Idempotence is deferred (acknowledged in commit `3b0b11e`)

`run()` always creates new `Evidence` and `Finding` rows; re-running a ScanTargetRun multiplies rows. Tracked as `#82` in the slice-7 commit message; needs `(scan_run, target, asset_url, map_url)` uniqueness or a per-run upsert. **Not blocking** for slice-7 close because Phase 1 stubs 1.1–1.13 have the same pattern (idempotence is a cross-cutting refactor, not a per-stub one).

### Test files exceed 200-line cap

`tests/test_validator.py` is 274 lines (over by 74); `tests/test_fetcher.py` is 205 (over by 5); `tests/test_runner.py` is 201 (over by 1). Per CLAUDE.md the cap applies to tests too. Candidate splits: `test_validator.py` → `{test_validator_shape.py, test_validator_metadata.py, test_validator_path_categories.py}`; the other two are border-cases — single-line splits don't justify a new file.

### `stale` status unused

`FindingStatus.STALE` exists in the enum but `classify_map_result` never emits it. Spec §"Finding status rules" (or its eventual enrichment) presumably mandates `stale` when the asset 404s on a re-scan after a confirmed finding — needs cross-run state. Deferred alongside idempotence.

### Severity ceiling baked into classifier

`_confirmed` raises severity to `LOW` only when `has_sources_content` or `internal_path_indicators` fire. `Severity.MEDIUM`+ would need a "shared deterministic secret detector" per the validator comment — not implemented. Baked policy choice; document explicitly when the spec is enriched.

### `version: int | None` accepts whatever the body says

`_as_int` returns `None` for string `"3"` (which the docstring acknowledges some bundlers emit). The validator preserves the raw value when it's a Python `int`. Spec §"Source map fetch" presumably pins `version==3` as a hard requirement; current code is permissive. Decide at enrichment time whether `version != 3` should downgrade confidence or reject.

## Implicit contract — backfill

To unblock a future spec-enrichment pass, here's what the implementation effectively contracts. Treat this as a starting draft for the `##` sections in `01-information-gathering/14-source-maps.md`.

**Purpose.** Detect publicly-exposed JavaScript and CSS source maps. Public `.map` files leak original module paths, framework conventions, and (when `sourcesContent` is included) the unminified source code itself — a passive information-gathering primitive that helps the operator map a target's stack and identify high-value attack surface without active exploitation.

**Inputs.** A `ScanTarget` with `base_url`. No credentials, no config knobs at the spec level — runner internals expose `FetcherConfig(max_body_bytes, max_redirects, timeout_seconds)` and `parse_html_assets(max_assets)` with cookbook-aligned defaults.

**Detection logic.** GET `base_url` (normalised to trailing-slash). Parse HTML for same-origin `<script src>` / `<link rel=stylesheet>` / `<link rel=modulepreload>` / `<link rel=preload as=script>`. For each asset (up to 50): GET, look for `//# sourceMappingURL=` (JS, both `#` and `@` accepted) or `/*# sourceMappingURL= */` (CSS). If present, resolve and probe the map URL with `reference_type="comment"`. If absent, single fallback probe `<asset>.map` with `reference_type="fallback"`. Cross-origin map URLs → `cross_origin` reject. `data:` URLs → `inline_data_url` candidate (no decode). Map body parsed as Source Map v3 (top-level object with `version` + at least one of `sources`/`sections`/`mappings`).

**Persistence.** Evidence row per HTML/asset/map GET (`source` = HTML | SCRIPT | CSS | PATH). One Finding per (asset, attempted-map) pair with `status ∈ {candidate, confirmed, rejected}`, `confidence ∈ {low, medium, high}`, `severity ≤ LOW`. `data` carries asset+map URLs, reference-type, indicators list, and Source Map v3 metadata when valid.

**Safety.** Read-only HTTP only. No body decoding for `data:` URLs. `sourcesContent` payload never persisted — only counts and a presence flag. No hostname-based heuristics. No mutating methods. No AI.

**Pass/fail check.** Positive: comment-referenced valid v3 map → confirmed/high; fallback-probed valid v3 map → confirmed/medium; inline `data:` → candidate; 404/410 on fallback → rejected. Negative: cross-origin map URLs never become confirmed; `sourcesContent` payload never written to evidence; no asset fetched if its URL is cross-origin with the base.

**Test fixtures.** `juice-shop` is the natural Phase 1 fixture (Angular bundle with `.map` files at predictable paths). DVWA and WebGoat have zero or no relevant assets — those fall into the "no findings" diagnostic-evidence path.

**Acceptance criteria.** Idempotent (deferred — see `#82`), deterministic, bounded by config caps, transport-error tolerant, redirect-policy compliant, no flaky retries.

## Verdict

**Implementation is sound** against the three axes the audit could measure (internal coherence, cookbook patterns, domain best practice). The code reads cleanly, tests cover positive + negative paths, 100% line+branch coverage on `apps/stubs/source_maps/` (verified by full suite run `1027 passed, 39 skipped`). The split into `runner / runner_evidence / runner_findings / classify / fetcher / parser / resolver / validator / path_categories` mirrors the slice-by-slice spec sections naturally.

**Stub closure is gated on spec enrichment** — frontmatter should remain `status: pending` until `14-source-maps.md` is filled in. The implementation is ready; the docs are the bottleneck. Once enriched, this review can be re-run against the real contract and the frontmatter flipped to `done`.
